criteria.criterion: In the real browser, a user can submit a representative case with a $500,000 starting portfolio, 30-year horizon, 3% inflation, and a supported positive desired ending balance; the page renders one verified first-year annual withdrawal, its supporting catalog allocation, and a 30-row projection ending at or above the requested balance.

For a representative $1,000,000 starting-portfolio case, the page states that the reported withdrawal is the highest verified amount across the disclosed finite catalog of fixed illustrative allocations, and increasing it by $0.01 fails the ending-balance floor for that winning allocation.

A desired ending balance is a projection constraint: negative values are rejected with an actionable message, while a balance above the starting portfolio is accepted when at least one catalog allocation verifies it under the deterministic model.
All money accepted, computed, stored, and rendered in the legacy-withdrawal path is integer cents end to end; the solver, projection, allocation, and UI do not use floating-point currency values.
Invalid-input and no-verified-result submissions clear any prior legacy-withdrawal result, allocation, and projection before showing an actionable refusal.
The feature remains product-only: it adds no runtime dependency, uses no live-provider data, changes no factory or CI files, and produces identical output for identical inputs.

For the current curated list, the solver canonicalizes total returns to product-owned thousandth-decimal rates, evaluates the resulting 23 fixed allocation catalog entries with a proven monotone integer-cent search rather than a per-cent sweep, and the representative Chrome-style browser flow renders in under 1 second.
